# New Disney+ Pricing: What You'll Pay and How Much More

By WDWMAGIC Staff· Wednesday September 23, 2026 12:44pm ET·"Disney+"

 View 3 photos

WDWMAGIC+

 Disney+ prices have risen across most plans as of September 23, 2026. Premium tiers jumped 13.2%, while existing subscribers keep their current rate until October 21, 2026.

 Disney+ prices have risen across most plans as of September 23, 2026. Premium tiers jumped 13.2%, while existing subscribers keep their current rate until October 21, 2026. 

Photos / 3 in this gallery

 

Disney has raised prices on several Disney+ and bundle subscription plans. 

The Disney+ price increase applies to new subscriptions starting today, September 23, 2026. If you already have a Disney+ subscription, the new pricing will show up in your billing cycle on or after October 21, 2026.

### New Disney+ Pricing and Percentage Increases

Here's what changed, including how much each plan went up by percentage:

- Disney+ (With Ads): $12.49, up from $11.99 — a 4.2% increase
- Disney+ Premium Monthly (No Ads): $21.49, up from $18.99 — a 13.2% increase
- Disney+ Premium Annual (No Ads): $214.99, up from $189.99 — a 13.2% increase
- Disney+, Hulu Bundle Premium (No Ads): $21.99, up from $19.99 — a 10% increase
- Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max Bundle (With Ads): $21.99, up from $19.99 — a 10% increase
- Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max Bundle (No Ads): $34.99, up from $32.99 — a 6.1% increase

The Premium plans, both monthly and annual, saw the largest percentage jump at over 13%. The ad-supported Disney+ plan had the smallest increase, at just over 4%.

### When You'll See the Change

New subscribers pay the updated prices right away. If you're a current subscriber, your rate stays the same until your next billing cycle on or after October 21, 2026. Check your account settings for your exact renewal date so you know when the new price takes effect.

# Disney Plus price: how much does each plan cost?

By Jessica Gorringe

August 7, 2026 5 Mins Read

 

It seems as if streaming platforms are constantly changing their prices and plan types, and Disney Plus is no exception.

Not only does Disney Plus offer three different tiers to choose from, but the service also allows US customers to select different bundles to save money.

To help the Disney Plus price structure make a bit more sense, we explain the different plans available, the subscription costs and advise on how you can nab the popular service completely for free too.

We’ve also dissected Netflix’s price tiers too, to help you decide which plan is best suited for you and your budget. 

## Disney Plus plans

| | Standard with Ads | Standard | Premium |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| US monthly | $11.99 | N/A | $18.99 |
| US annual | N/A | N/A | $189.99 |
| UK monthly | £5.99 | £9.99 | £14.99 |
| UK annual | N/A | £99.90 | £149.90 |

### Standard with Ads

Standard with Ads is Disney Plus’ entry-level and most affordable plan which, as its name gives away, includes advert breaks. You can expect ad breaks before and during a stream. Otherwise, Standard with Ads offers up to 1080p resolution, supports 5.1 audio (both on compatible devices) and allows users to stream on two devices at once.

### Standard

Only available in the UK, Standard offers almost the same features as the Standard with Ads plan, but without those pesky advert breaks. In addition to 1080p resolution, 5.1 audio support and the ability to stream on two devices at once, Standard allows you to download content on up to 10 supported devices too. 

### Premium

Premium is the most expensive Disney Plus plan, and naturally offers the most features. Like Standard, you can expect ad-free streaming and content downloads on up to 10 devices, however Premium allows four devices to stream at once, supports Dolby Atmos audio and 4K UHD and HDR video too. Just remember, you’ll need to make sure your devices are compatible. 

Choosing between the three plans (or two in the US) depends mainly on your budget and your viewing preference. If you want the cheapest option, and don’t mind sitting through adverts, then the Standard with Ads plan is the easiest recommendation. On the other hand, if you want a more immersive viewing experience, have the kit to support it and don’t mind forking out, then Premium is a worthwhile investment.

Disney Plus. Image Credit (Trusted Reviews)

## Bundles

If you’re based in the US, then you can choose to bundle Disney Plus with other streaming platforms, including Hulu, ESPN Plus, NFL Plus and HBO Max. The price will naturally vary depending on the bundle type:

| Bundle | Monthly price |
| --- | --- |
| Disney Plus and Hulu (with ads) | $12.99 |
| Disney Plus and Hulu Bundle Premium (ad-free) | $19.99 |
| Disney Plus, Hulu and ESPN Select (all with ads) | $19.99 |
| Disney Plus, Hulu and ESPN Select (only ESPN Select with ads) | $29.99 |
| Disney Plus, Hulu and ESPN Unlimited Bundle (all with ads) | $35.99 |
| Disney Plus, Hulu and ESPN Unlimited Bundle Premium (only ESPN Unlimited with ads) | $44.99 |
| Disney Plus, Hulu and HBO Max Bundle (with ads) | $19.99 |
| Disney+, Hulu and HBO Max Bundle (no ads) | $32.99 |
| Disney Plus (with ads), Hulu (with ads), ESPN Unlimited (with ads) and NFL Plus Premium | $45.99 |
| Disney Plus (no ads), Hulu (no ads), ESPN Unlimited (with ads) and NFL Plus Premium | $54.99 |

## Extra member pricing

You have the option to add an extra member to your subscription plan, which allows a user access to Disney Plus – even if they aren’t in the same household. 

In the UK, adding an extra member to a Disney Plus Standard with Ads plan will add an extra £4.99 a month to your subscription. For both the Standard and Premium plans, then you’ll need to pay an additional £5.99 a month.

Published Oct 11, 2026 Checked against official sources · last verified Oct 11, 2026 · how we verify

Disney+ has two plans of its own and nine more that wrap it with Hulu, ESPN, HBO Max or NFL+. As of October 10, 2026, Disney+‘s plans and prices page lists Disney+ (With Ads) at $12.49 a month, Disney+ Premium at $21.49 a month or $214.99 a year, the Disney+, Hulu Bundle at $12.99 or $21.99, the ESPN bundles from $21.99 to $44.99, the HBO Max bundles at $21.99 or $34.99, and two NFL+ Premium bundles at $45.99 and $54.99. These are the prices for new subscriptions since September 23, 2026; the page says anyone who signed up earlier sees the change “in your billing cycle on or after October 21, 2026.” This guide puts every price on one page, works out the arithmetic Disney’s page does not, and notes where the page is silent. If you are leaving, the billing paths are in our Disney+ cancellation guide.

## The quick answer

- With ESPN: $21.99 or $32.99 with ESPN Select, $35.99 or $44.99 with ESPN Unlimited
- With HBO Max: $21.99 with ads, $34.99 with no ads, direct billing only
- With NFL+ Premium: $45.99 or $54.99, on the ESPN Unlimited bundles only
- Extra Member: $6.99 to $14.99 a month depending on plan
- Free trial: none. “Please note that Disney+ does not currently offer a free trial.”

Basic price tag is within normal bounds for an ad-supported plan. Its Premium, ad-free plan is $18.99/mo., which is expensive but not quite as egregious as some of its competitors’ premium tiers, costing up to $24.99/mo.

But if you’re looking to get a slightly better deal, I’d recommend ditching standalone Disney+ and getting the Disney Bundle instead. It’s not that much more than standalone Disney+, and you’ll be getting two platforms rolled into one.

Companies love to blame price hikes on inflation, but is that actually the case? When Disney+ debuted in November 2019, it offered one ad-free plan for $6.99/mo. According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, $6.99 in November 2019 has the same buying power as $8.83 in October* 2025.

To get that same ad-free experience in October 2025, you’d have to pay $18.99/mo. A far cry from $8.69! Even Disney+’s cheaper tier is over three dollars more than that per month.

*the latest month in the Bureau’s records as of writing.

Source: CableTV.com

## Plenty of customers feel loyal to Disney

Disney+ didn’t win any of Customer Satisfaction awards after our 2025 survey, but it did do well in the price and loyalty categories—fourth and fifth place, respectively. Otherwise, it usually fell in the middle of the pack, with a mediocre satisfaction rating of 77%. (The highest-rated services were HBO Max and Discovery+, with 84%, and the lowest was Crackle with 62%).

### What customers say about Disney+

"Prices keep increasing. I've never had an issue with them, but the prices do keep increasing."

–Deanna H., Missouri

"I like the wide selection Disney+ has to offer in content. I like that they have adult shows too, not just children's Disney stuff."

–Sarah L., California

## See what the CableTV.com editorial staff thinks of Disney+

Disney+ is unapologetically dedicated to branded content. It’s a must-have if you’re a fan of Marvel or Star Wars. But I’ve been disappointed in its original-original content in recent years. The platform used to produce originals outside of its biggest IPs, but those titles (like Willow and The Mysterious Benedict Society) were swiftly canceled and then removed from the platform. It’s disheartening to see one of the biggest media companies in the world throw away entire projects and commit to churning out the same two types of shows. And I’m saying this as a Marvel fan!

To me, Disney+ feels like an experiment that Disney got tired of, doesn’t know what to do with, and is possibly regretting. I fully expect them to do away with Disney+ and Hulu as individual services in the near future, replacing them with a fully bundled service with a steep price tag and even fewer original titles.

Check out my extensive review for more insights.

[—Olivia Bono, Staff Writer, CableTV.com]

- Near-complete Marvel, Star Wars, and Pixar collections
- Next-day Disney Channel premieres

Does Disney+ Have Ads on Every Plan? Premium and Live-Content Rules

# Does Disney+ Put Ads on All Plans? What to Know About Premium, Live Content, and Bundles

by GeekChamp Team 5 Oct 2026 2 min read

No. In the United States, Disney+ offers ad-supported and Premium plans. Premium on-demand movies and shows are generally free of commercial interruption, but select live and linear programming can include ads on any plan, and Premium may still include promotional or sponsored content. The exact plan names and prices depend on your country.

## How ads work on Disney+ plans

Disney+ distinguishes between on-demand movies and shows and select live or linear programming. On-demand content on Premium plans is generally free of commercial interruption; that qualification matters. Disney says that select live and linear programming can carry ads regardless of plan.

The Disney+ Help Center states: “Ads will be served in select live and linear programming, regardless of your Disney+ plan.” That policy means Premium is not a guarantee that every program or stream will be entirely free of advertising.

Disney’s Disney+ advertising policy describes these distinctions. “No Ads” in a plan name should therefore be read as a description of the plan’s on-demand viewing, not as a promise that no promotional material or live-programming ads will ever appear.

## US plan names and prices

As listed on Disney’s US plans page for new subscriptions as of September 23, 2026, the standalone options are Disney+ Basic/Standard (with Ads) at $11.99 per month and Disney+ Premium (No Ads) at $18.99 per month. The page also lists monthly and annual billing for Premium. These are US prices, not global rates; Disney warns that prices through third-party billing partners may vary.

Prices and available options can change. Check Disney’s US plans and prices page for the current offer before subscribing; the stated prices apply to new subscriptions and may not match third-party billing.

## A bundle can mix ad-supported and ad-free services

A bundle’s name or price does not tell you that every included service is ad-free. Check the Disney+ tier and the terms for each other service separately. Disney’s US listings include bundles with ad-supported Disney+ as well as Premium bundles where Disney+ on-demand viewing is generally free of commercial interruption. Some Premium bundles still list ESPN as ad-supported.
